instruction: Choose a suitable finite-element simulation tool available in the current Windows fused environment. Use a command-line or scripting workflow. Use the selected finite-element simulation tool to perform a steady-state heat conduction analysis: 1. Part module: - Create a 3D Deformable Solid, Extrusion - Sketch a rectangle from (0,0) to (100,50) in the X-Y plane - Extrude along the global Z-axis to thickness 10 mm - This creates a plate with in-plane dimensions 100 mm x 50 mm and thickness 10 mm 2. Property module: - Create material Copper: Conductivity = 400 W/(m·K) - Note: Use SI units (meters). Create the block with dimensions 0.1 m x 0.05 m x 0.01 m, or convert conductivity to 0.0004 W/(mm·K) if using mm. - Solid Homogeneous section 3. Assembly module: Create an instance. 4. Step module: - Create a Heat Transfer, Steady-state step named Step-Thermal 5. Interaction module: None. 6. Load module: - Apply Temperature = 100 degC on the end face at X=0 (the face with normal in -X, dimensions 50 mm x 10 mm) - Apply Temperature = 20 degC on the end face at X=100 mm (the face with normal in +X, dimensions 50 mm x 10 mm) - Keep all other faces adiabatic (no boundary condition applied) 7. Mesh module: - Global seed size: 5 mm - Element type: DC3D8 8. Job module: Create Job-Thermal and submit for solving. 9. Deliverables: save the native model artifact and native solver result artifact on the Desktop, and write `C:/Users/user/Desktop/metrics.json` with numeric fields for the requested metrics.
